name: The Cajun Navy
label: Louisiana boat owners rescue flood victims in Katrina and Harvey
summary: After Hurricane Katrina in 2005, volunteers with their own boats, many from Louisiana, went into flooded areas to pull stranded people out of the water. Volunteers from Louisiana drove to Texas with fishing boats, jon boats, airboats, canoes and kayaks in 2017 to rescue people trapped by Hurricane Harvey floods. They were unofficial and organized mostly through social media. One crew revived an elderly woman found in the water in Houston.
caveat: Sources describe the 2005 origin differently: ABC13 says the governor called on a group of 23 vessels and nearly 30 people, CBC says the network formed in New Orleans, and Garden & Gun describes volunteers in Plaquemines Parish. No source here gives a verified total of people rescued in either storm.
